samir: Heads-up: noticed inconsistent behavior between Java and Kotlin SDKs around cancellation + retries on Android 13. Kotlin sampleapp cancels fine, Java sampleapp leaves leaked calls in dispatcher.

kevin: Interesting. Which layer is different? Retrofit CallAdapter, OkHttp interceptor, or our SDK wrapper?

samir: Traced it to our SDK helper that wraps Retrofit Call into a CompletableFuture (Java) vs suspend wrapper (Kotlin). Java path used future.cancel(true) -> underlying call.cancel(), but we also had a retry interceptor that re-enqueued call on certain 5xx. That re-enqueue logic didn't check call.isCanceled() on the Java path because of subtle timing.

anjali: Can you paste the retry snippet?

samir: ```java
// simplified
Response intercept(Chain chain) throws IOException {
  Response r = chain.proceed(chain.request());
  if (shouldRetry(r)) {
    // naive retry
    return chain.proceed(chain.request());
  }
  return r;
}
```

samir: In Kotlin we used a helper that checked coroutineContext.isActive before retrying and called call.isCanceled(). The Java path was missing that check. Result: after cancellation the retry interceptor still ran on worker threads and OkHttp dispatcher showed Running++ counts and eventual RejectedExecutionException under load.

kevin: Oof. So parity bug between SDK wrappers. Also calls re-proceeded after cancel, which is unexpected.

anjali: Another wrinkle: Android's ConnectivityManager can post callbacks to the main thread, and our Java future.cancel(true) ended up interrupting the thread running the retry decision, causing IllegalMonitorStateException in some internal code. Didn't see that on Kotlin since coroutines use cooperative cancellation.

samir: Repro steps I used:
  • Start emulator Android 13
  • Fire 30 concurrent requests through Java SDK wrapper with short deadline 1s
  • Make server return 503 first, then 200 after 2s
  • Cancel the future after 500ms for half of requests
  • Observe dispatcher: running increases, queued grows, and many tasks never complete.

kevin: Fix plan? Add parity: make Java wrapper use an explicit check of call.isCanceled() before retry and after catching IOException. Also avoid calling chain.proceed when the call is canceled. Use a shared helper used by both Java and Kotlin wrappers.

anjali: Also update docs: call.cancel() semantics and how interceptors should be idempotent and check for isCanceled. Add test in sampleapp that exercises cancellation races.

ci-bot: Created issue #4522: "SDK parity: Java wrapper permits retry after cancel -> dispatcher leaks" - https://git.internal/redwood/issues/4522 :warning:

samir: I pushed a small PR changing the retry interceptor to short-circuit on cancellation and updated the Java CompletableFuture wrapper to propagate cancel state earlier. Link: https://git.internal/redwood/sdk-java/pull/213

kevin: I'll review. Also, let's add a note in the migration doc: "If you implement a retry interceptor, ensure it respects call.isCanceled() and thread interruption semantics on Java futures; prefer cooperative cancel on coroutine paths."

anjali: For onboarding, add this tiny checklist entry: 1) avoid re-proceed after cancel 2) prefer coroutine-based wrapper on Android 3) include cancellation tests in CI.

doc-bot: Suggested docs update created: https://git.internal/redwood/docs/pull/78 - "Retry and cancel parity between Java and Kotlin SDKs"

samir: Thanks. I'll run a soak with the PR tomorrow and post results. Leaving this thread.
